title: Anti-GBM treatment: safer follow-up and separate timelines
summary: Follow a treated synthetic adult through infection prevention, leukopenia review, treatment planning and a transplant-timing discussion. Builds on the existing diagnostic and initial-treatment case.

stages.narrative: A synthetic 38-year-old has confirmed anti-GBM disease, negative ANCA and kidney failure. The specialist team has already started disease-directed treatment. At handover, the receiving clinician is asked to explain the safety plan.
prompts: Which observations follow response, and which can expose treatment harm?
What preventive care deserves consideration during cyclophosphamide and high-dose glucocorticoids?
teaching_points: Reveal: Follow kidney function, pulmonary findings, antibody titres and blood counts together. An improving symptom is only one part of the follow-up picture.

Reveal: Consider Pneumocystis prophylaxis with TMP-SMX alongside treatment of the autoimmune disease. The general recommendation is qualified by evidence largely from other immunosuppressed populations.

Reveal: Review infection risks in context. KDIGO lists TB, HBV, HCV, HIV and syphilis screening where clinically appropriate. Prior endemic residence with eosinophilia/elevated IgE raises a separate Strongyloides concern: glucocorticoids can precipitate dangerous hyperinfection from silent infection. These clues prompt assessment, not a diagnosis; risk assessment accompanies urgent care.

stages.narrative: Two weeks later, breathing is easier and anti-GBM titres are falling. A scheduled blood count identifies clinically significant leukopenia. The treatment chart has otherwise been carried forward unchanged.
prompts: Why is falling antibody activity insufficient reassurance?
What part of the plan now needs an active decision?
teaching_points: Reveal: Separate treatment response from tolerability. Blood-count surveillance can identify a safety problem even while organ disease improves.

Reveal: Review cyclophosphamide exposure promptly; leukopenia can require dose reduction or interruption. Use an individual specialist decision rather than inferring a safe numerical adjustment from this case.

stages.narrative: After the specialist team adjusts treatment, blood counts recover. At eight weeks, lung disease has resolved and circulating anti-GBM antibodies are undetectable. The person asks why the remaining medicines do not all finish together.
prompts: How do the usual treatment durations differ?
Which features would prevent applying a calendar plan mechanically?
teaching_points: Reveal: The usual responding course uses cyclophosphamide for 2-3 months and a glucocorticoid course of about 6 months with gradual tapering.
Reveal: Tolerability and disease activity still govern review. This framework does not prescribe drug doses, an abrupt steroid stop or a rescue regimen for persistent antibodies.

stages.narrative: At six months after diagnosis, kidney failure still requires dialysis. Anti-GBM antibodies have remained undetectable for four months since the eight-week review. The patient and a potential living donor ask whether transplantation can now occur.
prompts: Which date starts the relevant disease-specific interval?
What would reaching the interval establish, and what would still need evaluation?
teaching_points: Reveal: The interval is sustained undetectable anti-GBM antibodies, not elapsed time since diagnosis or the availability of a donor. Four months does not yet meet the at-least-six-month criterion.
Reveal: Continued assessment can plan ahead, but reaching the antibody interval is only one condition for transplantation. It is not a complete candidate or donor clearance.

stages.narrative: Debrief: You are preparing an educational handover that separates the reason for each treatment, the safety observations and the later transplant decision.
prompts: Explain why disease response, treatment safety and transplant timing cannot be reduced to one laboratory result.
Name a management decision that this teaching case leaves to an exact local protocol and specialist review.
teaching_points: Debrief: Keep response surveillance and blood-count safety review visible throughout treatment. Preventive infection care has a distinct purpose from suppressing antibody production.

Debrief: Keep the usual immunosuppressive course and the sustained-antibody-negative transplant interval separate. Numerical doses, renal/dialysis adjustments, prophylaxis regimens and refractory disease are outside this case.

take_home: A falling titre does not show that treatment is free of harm.
Use infection prevention as supportive care alongside disease-directed treatment.
Distinguish the usual drug-course durations from sustained antibody negativity before transplantation.
